Teen growth, decent FCF margin; the excitement is Base44 optionality, but the legacy website-builder business has too many sticking points and Base44 is compressing margin + raising acquisition-related payouts. decisions.rationale: Long-term compounder; seasoning unlocks cash flow as vintages amortize in line with underwriting; NIMAL exceptionally strong (~17.8% vs Nubank ~9.5%); Amazon-like logistics/real-world moat taking offline share; fine with negative net margin while incremental contribution margin is positive and they lean into share gains; cheap vs own history; <1 PEG on 2yr; re-rating -> 15-20% IRR over 3-5yr. Valuation frame: 40-50% revenue continuation + margins recovering to ~80% of prior peak, Amazon-at-scale comp, minus an international/country-risk haircut. Done adding.
decisions.falsifier: NIMAL sustained <13-14% (implies credit-book ROE <15%) OR realized losses on seasoned 2025+ vintages above provisions for 2+ quarters (underwriting breaks) OR incremental contribution margin turns negative (watch Mexico) / Brazil net margin fails to stabilize -> trim & reassess.

Revised thesis: 2026 is a price-driven trough not a structural top; beat the lowered -4/-12% CER bar on oral-Wegovy volume + international + pipeline; bad news priced at ~10x; broad portfolio (injectable+oral, global patents) spanning high-efficacy to lifestyle use cases. musings.body: My real operating philosophy: I'm a sentiment-washout buyer. I buy quality into sentiment lows - but the line between a 'washout buy' and a 'value trap' is the CATALYST TEST. Cheap + near-term catalyst + priced-in floor = buy (GOOG, MELI, RBRK, NVO). Cheap + no catalyst = trap (PYPL, KVYO, GTLB, WIX).
I keep selling winners too early - MU (sold ~$295, ~4x'd since), GOOG, TSM (trimmed the monopoly into strength). I underestimate how long momentum + earnings-power durability can run.

On my highest-conviction asymmetric bets I should keep the core but add a far-OTM long-dated LEAP sleeve - convex upside with defined (premium-capped) risk. I've regretted not doing this on MU and GOOG; NVDA is the live chance to actually do it.

Instrument-selection discipline: match the vehicle to the intent. Express a sector/macro theme via an index, not a single poorly-researched name (TORM). Hold dry powder in T-bills/SGOV, not a sector ETF that has its own drawdown (XLV). Express conviction via LEAPs.

AI-wave winners are CONSUMPTION/data-volume exposed, not seat-exposed. RBRK monetizes data volume (more agents -> more data -> more backup); GTLB/KVYO are seat/usage models the same wave could cannibalize. That's the real differentiator, not merely 'has a catalyst'.

My edge claim: the market misprices MELI's early credit provisioning and use of cash - the seasoning unlock is real IF realized losses track underwriting. Testable, and current data (margins compressing as the 87%-growth book stays young) partly cuts against it - track it as a live belief, not settled fact.

Calling NVO 'diversification away from tech' is a rationalization. A single -56% binary-catalyst pharma name adds idiosyncratic variance; it's merely uncorrelated to tech, not lower-risk. Own it as a contrarian alpha bet - true tech-diversification is a job for an ETF/LLY/basket. And respect my own note to diversify the GLP-1 THEME (Roche/AZN/Amgen/LLY) rather than concentrate the most-impaired name.

'The market is whack' is the most comfortable and most dangerous thing to say in a drawdown. Keep the verdict with the framework (my break-rules), not the feeling. NU's own leading indicator (15-90d NPL) is sitting on the 5% break line - Q2'26 decides whether the market was whack or early.

LatAm credit concentration: NU + MELI's credit book ~= $168k in the same LatAm consumer-credit cycle. Country mix (Brazil/Mexico/Colombia/Argentina) spreads idiosyncratic risk, but FACTOR risk (EM/FX/risk-appetite + the consumer-credit cycle) is doubled - they co-move in a risk-off.

Taiwan-conflict risk is shared by every fabless name that needs TSMC's capacity (NVDA, AVGO), so TSMC's discount to its fabless customers was an anomaly. That insight largely played out (TSMC re-rated). TSMC is the lowest-controversy, monopoly-priced way to own the whole AI buildout - a hold-the-core name.

NVDA 2-year hold: AI capex still rising and supply-constrained, multiple reasonable (~22-24x), but the 2-year risk is a 2027 capex digestion + accelerating custom-ASIC inference share - a multiple compression to the high-teens could pull the stock to the $150s even on rising EPS. The right way to own it may be a LEAP overlay, not just stock.
In a retirement account there's no loss-harvest benefit, so a depressed quality-ish name (trading ~1x FCF) is worth letting ride for the recovery rather than capitulating.

CPNG was a catalyst-test FAILURE I entered anyway - I forced my bottomed-out washout narrative onto a low-conviction name with no near-term catalyst (just 'regulatory headwinds dissipating'). The exit discipline worked (I cut fast once it was clear there was no catalyst), but the real lesson is on the ENTRY: the catalyst test must pass BEFORE I buy, not after. Following a company for a while is not a thesis.

themes.title: Sentiment-washout buyer (catalyst test)
themes.description: Buy quality into sentiment lows only when there's a near-term catalyst + priced-in floor; cheap-without-catalyst is a value trap to avoid. The dominant operating philosophy. CPNG is the instructive FAILURE case - forcing the narrative onto a no-catalyst name.

themes.title: Sells winners too early -> express via LEAPs
themes.description: Recurring tendency to book gains before momentum/earnings-power is exhausted; antidote is a core + far-OTM long-dated LEAP overlay on high-conviction names.

themes.title: Match the vehicle to the intent
themes.description: Sector/macro themes via an index not single stocks; dry powder in T-bills/SGOV not sector ETFs; conviction via LEAPs.

themes.title: LatAm fintech & commerce
themes.description: Concentrated LatAm consumer-credit + commerce exposure; country-diversified but factor-correlated (EM/FX/credit cycle).

themes.title: AI compute buildout (picks & shovels)
themes.description: Own the AI-capex supercycle via the indispensable layers - memory, foundry monopoly, full-stack compute - weighing ASIC substitution + capex-cycle risk.

themes.title: Sticky-workflow software compounders
themes.description: Systems-of-record / specialized-workflow SaaS that's AI-resilient because adoption is driven by embedded rigor, not hype.

themes.title: Software washout vs value trap
themes.description: Distinguishes catalyst-bearing, consumption-exposed SaaS bought in a washout (buy) from good-but-catalyst-less, seat-exposed SaaS (avoid).

themes.title: GLP-1 / obesity
themes.description: Contrarian GLP-1 exposure via the beaten-down incumbent; the discipline is to diversify the theme rather than concentrate the most-impaired name.

themes.title: Distribution-advantaged AI & durable compounders
themes.description: Incumbents that reclaim AI value via distribution + full stack, and durable cash-compounders.

themes.title: Counter-cyclical / dry-powder sleeve
themes.description: Attempts to hold low-beta or counter-cyclical ballast as redeployable dry powder - lesson: use the right instrument (T-bills) not a sector ETF or single value stock.
